title: The gradient bandit and LinUCB
brief: Learn arm preferences by stochastic gradient ascent, confirm the update's expectation is the exact gradient, then use context features and confidence ellipsoids with LinUCB.
hints: The gradient bandit moves every arm: the pulled one by alpha * (r - b) * (1 - pi[arm]), and each other arm a by -alpha * (r - b) * pi[a]. np.eye(k)[arm] - pi covers both at once.
expected_update is a weighted sum: for each arm x, pi[x] times (gradient_bandit_update(H, x, q[x], baseline, 1.0) - H).
In run_gradient_bandit, compute the baseline before you fold the new reward into the running mean. Including the current reward makes the baseline depend on the arm you just pulled.
Sherman-Morrison: with u = A_inv @ x, the new inverse is A_inv - outer(u, u) / (1 + x @ u).
In run_linucb, update only the pulled arm: A_inv[arm] with sherman_morrison and b[arm] += reward * x.
